description_conclusion: The fixed numbered-list candidate has positive matched physical-gradient preference against plain answers in both seeds, but its sparse code is positive on only one of eight short items in seed 42 and three of eight in seed 43; both have zero code on all long semantic items. The fixed bullets candidate has zero code on every semantic item in both seeds and has negative mean bullet-versus-plain physical preference on short answers. These descriptions do not yet supply a robust, selective explanation of the new tasks.
causal_conclusion: The targeted named coefficient is zero in 16 of 16 batches for seed 42 and 11 of 16 for seed 43, including all bulleted batches in both seeds. Those removals and their zero-norm controls are literally unchanged updates and cannot establish causal necessity. The five nonzero numbered removals in seed 43 have tiny effects: averaged over numbered batches, numbering falls by 0.0488 percentage points, with a pointwise question/block interval of -0.293 to 0 points. Single-atom interventions change length in both signs and seeds. The seed-42 numbered candidate at strength +1 increases bullets by 2.44 points and numbering by only 0.391 points, while adding 0.522 tokens. Format shifts remain confounded; no label is retrospectively promoted to a validated verbosity feature.
forecast_conclusion: Primary calibration-transfer dictionary content/order nRMSE is 1.015/0.999, with pointwise intervals 0.984-1.119/0.991-1.011. Numbering nRMSE is 0.994/1.000 and bullets 1.000/0.998. Named-only forecasts are effectively no change. Dictionary mean token-change predictions are +0.054/+0.019 versus actual +3.621/+1.744. All primary methods predict zero additional truncation despite actual mean increases of 1.59/0.684 percentage points. There is no convincing primary atom forecast or named-atom explanation in this development study.
secondary_conclusion: The complete dictionary retains some same-question numerical signal: content/order nRMSE 0.896/0.750; the seed-43 pointwise interval is 0.589-0.974, and seed 42 includes one. Same-question token nRMSE is 0.917/0.867. These use evaluation-question proposal profiles and do not validate the primary calibration transfer or the descriptions of the named atoms. No comparison against SVD or full gradients is a success requirement. All task/style tails, missing events, probability-range violations and no-effect edits are retained.
next_development: Investigate the atom encoding before another prospective generation study. Freeze a separate retrospective diagnostic of original Lasso, an unshrunk least-squares refit on exactly its active support, fixed OMP16, and a dense least-squares dictionary-span reference, using all cached batch projections and the same frozen dictionary. Select no penalty or support using observed behavioral outcomes. Measure reconstruction, magnitude, named-atom inclusion and coefficient stability. Recomputed historical forecasts must remain labeled retrospective development diagnostics. Any later prospective test still needs fixed held-out descriptions, selective interventions, separate calibration and independent evaluation, and newly locked forecasts. Do not promise a positive result or expand proposal banks as a generic cure.
not_confirmation: Four content blocks and four task families, two reused adapters and previously inspected broad task types; pointwise descriptive intervals only. No fresh-seed untouched-data confirmation or broad interpretability claim.
